extracted.intended_audience: general readers and historians interested in the North-West Mounted Police and late-19th-century Canadian western history
extracted.subtask_description: A popular-historical account (book chapter) describing the duties, conduct, and social role of the North-West Mounted Police in late 19th-century Western Canada, including incidents, recommendations, and reflections on policy. The page mixes narrative episodes with prescriptive remarks and official-report quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police–missionary partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: In the partnership of the Police and the missionaries the law and the gospel wrought together for good ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collaboration with missionaries to help preserve peace among Indigenous populations; missionaries' influence (e.g., John McKay) could prevent chiefs joining rebellions and promote reconciliation (example: Mistawasis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat prisoners with dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: It was a graceful recognition of his gallantry that the authorities at the penitentiary, at the instance of the Department, left the fine locks of their captive unshorn during his prison term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show respect for worthy qualities of captives (e.g., Poundmaker's unshorn hair) to maintain dignity and goodwill; small acts of consideration are positive policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward and recognize loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: At the suggestion of the Mounted Police officers many of the chiefs who had remained loyal were taken on a tour of the east, where they received many tokens of the kindly attitude of Canadians towards them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly reward loyal Indigenous leaders (e.g., tours, tokens) to strengthen bonds and promote future cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police as guides for settlers (social service role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Police showed that they were in the country not only to preserve law and order but to guide settlers in the interests of the country's development as well as for their own welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in non-policing guidance: teach good farming practices, advise on local resources, and help settlers avoid common mistakes (examples: fall ploughing, appropriate land use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural advice / good farming practice
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule too little fall ploughing is done in the North-West, and there is consequently too much hurry amongst the farmers in the spring... Very few of them made any use of the manure from their farmyards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate fall ploughing, prudent land allocation ('nearly all the farmers work too much land for their strength'), and use of manure and fertilizers; police reports could (and did) promote sound agricultural reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt appropriate local industrial contracts (fuel/coal)
rubrics_metrics.description: This could be avoided by entering into coal contracts with people residing near the coal beds on the North Saskatchewan, who would be able to supply at low rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend local procurement (e.g., coal contracts) to reduce fatigue, waste and expense—practical logistical recommendations to improve force efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and maintain detailed official reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the most remarkable and important documents sent forward to the proper authorities... were written by the surgeons and their assistants, and also by the veterinary surgeons... their reports bore the evidences of research, which made them treasuries of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage meticulous, research-quality reporting from medical and veterinary staff as well as commanders—these reports serve as valuable records and sources of insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build trust through fair play
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers and men of the Police had from the beginning so commended themselves to the Indians and half-breeds as exponents of fair play that these natives of the country never seemed to hold the Police responsible for the errors, delays or mistakes of any government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct policing with fairness to win local confidence; fair treatment separates the force's reputation from government errors and aids long-term order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence in law enforcement despite local sympathy for accused
rubrics_metrics.description: There seems to be an absurd idea that the dismissal of a charge means a snub to the Mounted Police, whereas it strikes home at the root of society and threatens the lives and property of the very men who jeer and flaunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue convictions and discourage petitions that lessen penalties; recognize the societal danger of leniency born of sympathy and work to secure justice even when local juries are sympathetic to defendants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough patrols to deter and capture criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Perry and his detachments... so combed the whole country in search of the perpetrators that this attempt to introduce the Jesse-James programme into Canadian territory was effectually discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exhaustive, energetic patrols and searches to discourage organized or copycat crimes (example: combing the country after a stage robbery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt public-safety response and search procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A Police party was dispatched to search the neighbourhood... The child was found... beyond being somewhat frightened, was little the worse for the exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize prompt search-and-rescue actions, suspend routine comforts when needed, and use practical search patterns (e.g., holding hands and swinging in compass circles) to ensure complete coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use veterinary expertise and decisive biosecurity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The horses appeared to be glandered, he wired for Veterinary Surgeon Wroughton... who declared the case virulent, and ordered everything destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call veterinary specialists on suspect disease, and when necessary carry out destruction of infected animals to prevent spread; follow expert orders even if difficult, and expect to seek compensation for losses (example: slaughter of glandered horses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote education and industrial training for Indigenous youth
rubrics_metrics.description: The hope of improvement in the Indian lies in the training of the rising generation... Perry's recommendation then made as to Industrial Schools bore fruit not many years later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support and implement educational and vocational programs (industrial schools) as a long-term strategy to enable Indigenous self-support and social improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and assist half-breeds to take up farming
rubrics_metrics.description: The mass of the half-breed population must therefore turn their attention to other methods of making a living. ... farming must become their occupation in earnest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urge, encourage and aid half-breed communities to remain on holdings and adopt farming, treating them with patience and providing instruction and generous assistance to adapt to settled agriculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use persuasion rather than force to suppress cultural practices
rubrics_metrics.description: There was nothing in the festival that would justify a forcible suppression of it... the Mounted Police used their persuasive influence against it and showed the younger Indians how foolish and useless it was.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid forcible suppression of cultural/religious practices where possible; prefer persuasion, example and gradual social influence to discourage harmful customs (example: Sun-dance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt new technology to improve efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction of the telephone would lead to an enormous saving of men and horses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wherever feasible, deploy communications and other technologies (telephone) to reduce manpower strains and increase operational effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain high selection standards and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: "I want to see the Mounted Police Force to be the hardest to get into and the easiest to get out of in the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep entry standards high and make retention contingent on conduct; discourage desertion and maintain a disciplined, reputable corps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster social/community events to build goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: The barrack hall was thrown open on occasion for winter gatherings... to teach people to enjoy proper recreation and play is to make them better citizens and more cordial one to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize sports, races and social evenings to integrate the Force with local communities and provide positive alternatives to violent or 'barbaric' customs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise firearm restraint; use proportionate force
rubrics_metrics.description: With the usual Police restraint they forbore to shoot... Campbell fired in the air, but Berube kept going, whereupon Campbell shot the smuggler's horse, and the patrol took Berube... of course they followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid shooting people where possible; use warning shots and target animals or other non-lethal measures only as necessary to effect capture—demonstrate restraint, but be prepared to act decisively when justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-border cooperation and reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: The relations existing between the Mounted Police and the American soldiery south of the line were always of the most cordial and fraternal type... This was the only opportunity I had to reciprocate the courtesy so freely extended to us under similar circumstances by the American officers at that post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain cordial, reciprocal relations with neighboring forces to enable mutual assistance (example: returning a horse to American officers).
